title: Street vendors' calls and wake singers
summary: He recalls blues and laments from wake-goers and imitates the peddlers' street calls.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, I hear these wakemen passing, they just had to pass in front of the door, in front of the... This tenement, not him, coming from wake, singing blues and laments. I see these blind men... passing by... in these... street calls and chants. I heard most of the peddlers when their voice were real ripe before they wore out late on the day. Out here when they came out fresh with their vegetable wagons.
Whatever... Whatever... Things that were sold, they were advertising in this unique way. Like, for instance, they had a load of bananas. Y'all like...
Lady, I've got bananas. Y'all a bananas, lady. Twenty-four nickels. And if you're pretty, I might give you twenty-five, madam.
Y'all was emphasizing. There was always a little human, those... street calls. Ah... They were selling stonko, no idea to tell you.
I've got stonko, lady. Come get the stonko before you freeze the bed, madam. Come on, get this stonko. Come on, get this stonko.
